title: The setting sun
hookLine: the first visualization: the setting sun, like a drum hung in the west

cards: How do I see it? That was the queen's question, and it's a hard one. The land of bliss lies in the west, and nobody can walk there or look there.
So the Buddha's first answer is almost startling in how plain it is. No chant. No doctrine.
No secret. He tells her to look at something anyone can see on a clear evening: the sun, going down in the west.

teach.b: First, the instruction. In the meditation sutra, the Buddha tells Vaidehi to sit facing west and look at the sun as it's about to set.
Fix the mind on it, he says, steadily, without letting the thought wander anywhere else. Second, the image.

teach.h: A DRUM HANGING IN THE SKY.
teach.b: As the sun sinks, the sutra says, it looks like a drum hanging in the sky: round, full, still, hung in the west. Then the real work: hold that image clear, whether the eyes are open or closed. The sunset ends.
The drum stays. The sutra calls this the first meditation, the perception of the sun. Third, why the sun.
Every evening the setting sun points west, toward the land of bliss.

teach.h: THE ONE THING ANYONE CAN SEE.
teach.b: So the first step toward a land no one can see starts from the one thing anyone can see. In Japanese this practice is called nissokan, the sun contemplation. Fourth, where it leads.

teach.h: THE FIRST RUNG OF A LADDER.
teach.b: The sun is only the first rung of a ladder. The meditations that follow climb, one image at a time, from things the eyes know toward the land itself, and toward Amitabha.
Each image steadies the mind enough to hold the next. Tomorrow's rung is water.
For today, the whole practice fits in one evening: a window facing west, and a sun hung like a drum, held in mind after the light is gone.

how: Following the meditation sutra, some Pure Land practitioners sit facing west at sunset and hold the image of the setting sun in mind; in Japanese this is called nissokan, the sun contemplation.

o: a sign that the day's practice should now come to an end
the first meditation: hold the sinking sun like a drum
the Buddha's own death, pictured as a sun going down

a list of rules to keep.
games.why: the first meditation is the plainest: the setting sun, like a drum hanging in the west, held steady in the mind.

practice: If the sun is setting where you are, turn toward it without staring straight into it; if not, close your eyes and call up a sunset you remember.
Let the sun hang low and round in the west like a drum, and when the image fades or the mind drifts, gently bring the drum back. Nothing to add, nothing to figure out.

wordCard.voice: The setting sun. The first meditation given to Queen Vaidehi: sit facing west, look at the sinking sun like a drum hung in the sky, and hold the image with eyes open or closed. Today's word.

orig.note: Japanese: nissokan, the sun contemplation, the first of the meditations in the meditation sutra.

carryVoice: Your line: the drum in the west. The light goes; the image stays. See you tomorrow.
